To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best registration results for histological data can be obtained with TPS 3D warp, NEWUOA, and a correlation coefficient cost function.

(a) slice-to-volume registration of histological sections to MR images can be successfully performed using a variety of optimization algorithms, cost functions, and deformation fields, (b) TPS-based 3D warp, NEWUOA optimization, and correlation coefficient cost function yield the best registration results, (c) registration performance is highly dependent on the type of cost function, (d) the choice of optimization algorithm is less critical for registration performance, (e) the choice of deformation field is less critical
the proposed slice-to-volume registration algorithms can be successfully applied to cross-modally registered histological images of human brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development and evaluation of slice-to-volume non-rigid registration of histological sections to MR images of the human cortex.
a flexible framework for slice-to-volume non-rigid registration of histological images with 3D warp deformation fields parametrized by TPS, GEBS, or cubic B-spline functions.

the development of a flexible slice-to-volume registration framework and the evaluation of its performance for cross-modal registration of histological sections to magnetic resonance images of human brains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of cost function and optimization algorithm is more important than the choice of the geometric deformation model.
the best registration algorithm is a function of the particular application and data.
, for a particular application, the optimal registration algorithm should be chosen based on the type of images, the quality of the images, and the nature of the expected deformation field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

slice-to-volume registration is feasible, that it is possible to achieve good results, that the best results are obtained for a specific combination of cost function and optimization algorithm, and that the choice of a spline class for deformation field parametrization has a significant influence on the results.

the proposed slice-to-volume registration framework can be successfully used for cross-modal registration of histological slices to MR images, and it is flexible enough to be adapted to other types of histological data.
the best registration results were obtained with a 3D TPS deformation field and the NEWUOA optimizer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a flexible framework for registration of histological sections to MR images is feasible and provides good registration accuracy.
the slice-to-volume framework is an important step towards the development of automated quantitative methods for analysis of histological sections.

the proposed framework is flexible enough to accommodate a variety of optimization methods and cost functions and that it provides a good starting point for further investigation of slice-to-volume registration algorithms.
